newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe deports North Korean diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe deports North Korean diplomat.

text.p: Zimbabwe has deported a North Korean diplomat who was arrested last month on charges of illegally possessing ivory, a top government official said in remarks published on Thursday.

Home (Interior) Affairs permanent secretary Tinaye Chigudu told a local weekly newspaper that Jang Myong Sik, a counsellor at North Korea's embassy in neighbouring Zambia, was served with a deportation order last week at North Korea's Harare mission where he had been holed up since his arrest.
Jang was arrested on January 24 at Harare airport after security staff there searched his luggage and allegedly found 33 pieces of raw ivory.

Police released him to the North Korean embassy in Harare and said last week they were awaiting the government to advise them on how to handle the case and whether Jang's diplomatic immunity in Zambia extends to Zimbabwe.
"Jang was served with a deportation order last week and has since left the country. The ivory was confiscated by the state," Chigudu told the independent Financial Gazette.
"We did not want to cause any unnecessary wrangle with the DPRK (Democratic People's Republic of Korea) over this matter," he said.
Trade in ivory was banned worldwide in 1989. Under the law in Zimbabwe violaters could face up to five years in jail if convicted.
North Korean embassy officials have refused to comment on the issue.
